text:
ashley: noticed a weird failure mode in staging during the last load test — when the gateway evicts an upstream streaming connection mid-response we sometimes end up with a half-committed client stream and no clear fallback. users see a hanging spinner or a short gibberish partial.

raj: yup i've seen that. eviction is currently a blunt `RST` from the proxy to upstream + immediate client trailer with `grpc-status=13` in some cases. not good for idempotency or partial-progress semantics.

eve: is the problem that the gateway doesn't emit an explicit partial-response trailer? or that the client can't distinguish a truncated stream vs a transient retry?

ashley: both. client lib treats any midstream close as terminal unless there's an explicit resume token. but we don't have resume tokens for short-lived upstream eviction paths.

raj: quick thought: add an `x-rw-evict-hint: <evict-id>` header on the midstream trailer and a `resume-offset` when available. client can show partial output + offer retry with `evict-id` so server can correlate.

sam: sounds promising but how do we avoid memory blowups if we hold resume state for lots of evicted streams? we have limited K/V cache and retention budgets.

eve: proposal: only retain resume pointers for requests that hit a configured quality-of-progress checkpoint (e.g., every N tokens or when structured output boundary is reached). Otherwise fallback to cheap short-response variant.

ashley: agree. we can expose this as `progress_markers` config on the route. default = `boundary: sentences|tokens:100` and `ttl: 30s`.

raj: also need a clear client-visible status code so UX can show "partial result — retry available" vs "definitive error". suggest `grpc-status=8` + `x-rw-partial=true` trailer for partial.

sam: +1 but ops: how do we account billing/metrics? partial replays should not double-bill tokens unless replayed. we need a `evict-id` mapping to billed token range.

ops-bot: deploy queued: gateway/edge-proxy v1.42.3 -> canary (region us-west-2) (rolling) :rocket:

eve: minimal header sketch:```
Trailer: {
  x-rw-evict-id: abcd1234
  x-rw-resume-offset: 2048
  x-rw-partial: true
  grpc-status: 8
}
```
client flow: if `x-rw-partial` present -> surface partial + offer retry button. retry sends `x-rw-resume=abcd1234` header.

ashley: fallback variant: if resume state not found or TTL expired, gateway should route to `model-short` variant and append `x-rw-evict-fallback: true` so calling app knows we returned a short answer.

raj: tradeoffs: increases metadata surface and some state in control plane, but avoids opaque client failures. we should gate behind feature flag and add metric `edge.evict.partial` and `edge.evict.resumed`/`edge.evict.fallback`.

sam: also add an admission control rule: resume-state capacity consumed charged to tenant in units of mb-seconds. prevents noisy tenants from hogging retention.

eve: agree. ops runbook snippet: "If >5% evictions are resulting in fallbacks, increase pool or tune `progress_markers`". add alert `EVICT_FALLBACK_RATE > 5% for 10m`.

ashley: ok i'll open an RFC follow-up with the header/trailer contract, config knobs (progress_markers, resume_ttl, fallback_variant), and proposed metrics+billing change. will paste link here once created.

raj: thanks. can we also add tests for client-visible UX? fake a midstream RST and validate the client shows partial + retry token.

sam: +1. i'll coordinate load tests for the retention accounting too.

ashley: filing RFC: https://rfc.internal/r/evict-stream-resume-contract (draft) — comments welcome :eyes:

ops-bot: deploy succeeded: gateway/edge-proxy v1.42.3 canary -> 1/3 hosts (us-west-2) succeeded.
